name: Villa Borghese
title: Ancient Trees in Rome's Villa Borghese: 5 to Find
meta_description: Rome's largest park holds Adonis, a 425-year-old plane, the last of an 18th-century cypress planting, and three more remarkable trees.
intro: Cardinal Scipione Borghese built this park in the early 1600s as a showcase for his art collection, and his gardener planted the trees to match: oriental planes brought in as a novelty, arranged in a valley that still carries their name. Adonis, the oldest of them, has stood here for over four centuries and outlived the villa's original owner by nearly as long. A cedar leans over the lake a few minutes' walk away, and past the boating lake stands what one conservation group calls the last survivor of the eighteen cypresses planted around Piazza di Siena in 1789, the arena that still hosts Rome's international horse show every year. Deeper into the park's holm oak wood, behind the museum that now holds a de Chirico and Warhol collection, a pair of hackberries with a four-metre girth waits on the official monumental status that roughly thirty of the park's other old trees are still queuing for.
